(3) Count is blind to commercial validity — 30 bets at demo artificial prices against fake prices passes without proving real edge. Proposed replacement: **sequential evidence standard with four tiers, each a precondition for the next.** Tier 0 (Preconditions, must pass before evidence counting begins): EXP-017 Part B confirmed (real Kalshi prices show positive EV); price discovery confirmed using production API prices. Tier 2 (Model Performance Trends): realized win rate within ±15% of predicted probability; realized EV (P&L / wagered) positive; Brier score on paper bets ≤ 0.265 (within L1 drift threshold); **P&L slope trending positive over game nights** — not just net positive at sample end. Tier 3 (Risk Control): no bet exceeds per-event cap; drawdown never exceeds 15% during paper period; C4 rejection rate 20–80% (selectivity confirmed). Statistical floor: ≥50 resolved bets provides meaningful power; this is a floor for validity, not the gate itself. A bet count that passes the floor while failing any trend criterion is an automatic gate failure. A superseding APR (APR-XXXX) is required before this framework is operative. APR-0016 remains the active gate until superseded. T-113 registered. | DS |

Correct framing: (1) p_t4 is a fresh Poisson estimate from current game state; (2) p_t1 serves only two roles — the materiality gate (|p_t4 − p_t1| ≥ T4_MIN_DELTA_P required to act) and the fire condition reference (p_t4 > mip + vig). The "Bayesian" label was architectural baggage from early T4 design iteration, not a description of what the code does. Four corrections made: `game_state_model.py` module docstring (removed "Bayesian update / T1 prior" framing), `GameStateModel` class docstring (same), `T4Signal.p_t1` field comment ("benchmark" not "prior"), `T4Signal.p_t4` field comment ("fresh from game state; not a posterior"); and `run_t4_inplay.py` `GameStateEvent.p_t1` field docstring (clarified two-role usage). Fix: moved input processing *before* the draw, replaced single `getch()` with a drain loop (processes all queued keys per iteration), reduced `time.sleep(0.05)` → `time.sleep(0.016)` (~60fps). Because `bankroll_usd` in `paper_portfolio.json` is deducted at `open_position()` and credited back at resolution, deployed stakes appear as a loss. | 2026-06-09 | **[SESSION 40] ADR-0018 ACCEPTED: Band exit mechanics — symmetric filter-out for all execution bands (APR-0018)** | Operator mandate (Earl Ignacio, 2026-06-09 SESSION 40): "Each bucket not only has a filter into — but should have a filter out of, all using quantifiable strategies (with qual enhancers)." Trigger: G3 analysis revealed that T4 (and all current bands) have filter-IN logic (Poisson CDF entry signal, Kelly sizing, MIN_EDGE gate) but NO filter-OUT logic. When `p_t4` drops below `p_t1 - EXIT_THRESHOLD` and an open YES position exists, the system holds with no mechanism to exit — even when the same Bayesian math that fired the entry now argues against the position. Prediction markets are bilateral instruments: SELL YES and BUY NO are both valid exit mechanisms (Kalshi supports both). The system is not exploiting this. Architectural scope of filter-out: (1) **Exit trigger**: `p_t4 < p_t1 - EXIT_THRESHOLD` AND open YES position exists → evaluate exit; symmetric for NO positions. (2) **Exit instrument**: SELL YES or BUY NO (whichever is more favorable given current bid/ask). (3) **Exit sizing**: Kelly inverse — size the exit proportionally to the magnitude of the signal reversal. (4) **Qual enhancer**: T3 FADE signal amplifies exit decision (T3 FADE + Bayesian reversal = stronger exit case than either alone). (5) **Time gate**: no exits in final N minutes when bid/ask spreads widen and market is illiquid. (6) **Cost model**: only exit if E[loss from holding] > spread cost of exit — prevents churning on noise. Implementation targets: `paper_trader.py` (`exit_position()` method), `VenueAdapter` sell order type, `run_t4_live.py` exit path in `_run_cycle()`. NO changes to current open positions or anything deployed. ADR-0018 (Band Exit Mechanics) required before implementation. T-145 registered. | DS |

EXIT_NET_COST_FLOOR=0.0175 (taker fee at mip=0.50, worst case; spread excluded pending EXP-019C). Results at representative player (22 pts/game, adj_pace=0.458 pts/min): T1=0.22053 (statistical), T2=0.22053 (statistical), T3=0.22053 (statistical), T4=0.13905 (statistical), T5=0.13328 (statistical). T5 buffer (0.133) similar to T4: near-zero λ drives high PMF at k=1 (P(X=0)=exp(-λ)≈0.400), but low σ_λ=0.167 offsets it. Script: `scripts/run_exp019a_analytic.py`. All values are candidate values pending EXP-019A empirical validation (observed p_current variance in paper trajectories). EXP-019C spread data will push final values higher. T1/T2/T3 σ_λ values require empirical validation — geometric mean is a bounded estimate, not a measured posterior. | DS |

## Decision Principles

These principles guide all decisions in this project:

1. **No decision is reversible without a superseding ADR.** ADRs are immutable once accepted.
2. **"We'll fix it later" is a shadow commitment.** If it matters, log it as an open question or RID.
3. **Deferred decisions must have a named gate.** "TBD" without a deadline is a gap, not a decision.
4. **arb/ folder: gate is APR-0010, not momentum.** No incorporation without explicit approval.
5. **Live capital decisions require two artifacts:** a superseding ADR and a signed approval (APR-0009).

| 2026-05-22 | **[RETROACTIVE / T-154] CHANGE_CONTROL.md framework decisions extracted — three-tier classification, SKELETON→ACTIVE ADR requirement, no-emergency-override rule, conditional-language escalation rule** | T-154 governance hygiene pass. (1) **Three-tier change classification (Class A/B/C):** Adopted alongside ADR-0001 (Compass OS). Class A = ADR required + immutable record; Class B = CHANGELOG entry only; Class C = artifact update only. Rationale: changes that affect capital risk, compliance, or model behavior require the full deliberation artifact (ADR); tactical changes require only a record; administrative changes require only state update. (2) **SKELETON→ACTIVE promotion is Class A (ADR required), not Class B:** A band promotion without an ADR makes a live execution path silently active — equivalent to promoting a model version without ADR-0004 controls. Machine-readable `band_status` field in `BAND_REGISTRY` is what separates SKELETON (code runs, no bets) from ACTIVE (bets fire). An ADR is required because this is a capital-risk-bearing state change, not a documentation change. New strategy registration (no live capital) is Class B because no capital-bearing state change occurs at registration time. (3) **No emergency override path for risk limits:** If a risk limit needs urgent adjustment, the correct response is the kill switch (halt all activity) — not a temporary limit override. An emergency override path that bypasses ADR review would create a governance hole that could be used to rationalize risk increases under pressure. No such path was built and none should be. (4) **Conditional language in canonical registers must be escalated before session end — never deferred:** Conditional language ("may be revised", "subject to DS decision") that survives a context window transition looks like a resolved decision to the next context. This was observed in GG-001: a `# 10 concurrent open (stub)` comment survived four gate clearances. The escalation-before-session-end rule closes this class of failure. | DS |

| 2026-06-22 | **[SESSION 69] DS DECISION — Option C (feature-set diagnosis sprint) + DIAGNOSIS FINDINGS: anti-predictive edge driven by missing playoff-context λ multiplier, not model class failure** | **DS decision (Earl Ignacio, 2026-06-22 S69):** T-177 escalation path = **Option C — feature-set diagnosis sprint.** Not Option A (halt + ADR-0004 supersession) and not Option B (direction inversion — flagged as not trivially safe). Rationale: the anti-predictive edge is identifiable in the data as a specific feature engineering gap, making a model class change premature. T-072 (model retrain) may proceed in Phase 2 but targets the feature fix identified below, not a change of model architecture. **Diagnosis findings (n=103 clean bets, NBA Finals G2–G5, conducted S69):** Full feature-set breakdown run on `data/nba_finals_clean_dataset.csv` (is_clean=True). **Finding 1 — Direction asymmetry.** YES bets (n=36, edge>0): win rate 38.9%. NO bets (n=67, edge≤0): win rate 68.7%. YES/NO split is exact (edge>0 ≡ YES direction in this dataset). **Finding 2 — Model vs market calibration error.** YES bets: mean model_p=0.704, mean mip=0.539, actual win rate=0.389. Model error (model_p − actual): +0.315. Market error (mip − actual): +0.150. Market is 2.1× better calibrated on YES bets. NO bets: mean (1−model_p)=0.825, mean (1−mip)=0.693, actual win rate=0.687. Model error: +0.138. Market error: **+0.006** — Kalshi market is essentially perfectly calibrated on NO bets. **Finding 3 — Threshold amplification.** YES bets by threshold: thr=10 (model_p=0.893, mip=0.724, actual=0.643; model_err=+0.250, mkt_err=+0.081); thr=15 (model_p=0.642, mip=0.476, actual=0.250; model_err=+0.392, mkt_err=+0.226); thr=20 (model_p=0.493, mip=0.346, actual=0.222; model_err=+0.271, mkt_err=+0.123). The model's YES error worsens dramatically at thr≥15; at thr=15-20 both model and market overestimate but model is 2-3× worse. **Finding 4 — Implied λ compression.** Inverting model_p to recover the implied Poisson λ: at thr=10, model implies λ=14.0 but actual_pts=12.8 (compression=0.911); at thr=15, model implies λ=16.1 but actual_pts=12.8 (compression=0.792); at thr=20, model implies λ=19.6 but actual_pts=13.8 (compression=0.703). The model systematically assumes scoring rates ~10-30% higher than Finals reality. **Finding 5 — Within-series compression drift.** YES bet win rates by game: G2=71.4% (avg_pts=17.3), G3=25.0% (avg_pts=11.8), G4=41.7% (avg_pts=15.5), G5=22.2% (avg_pts=7.7). Scoring collapses across the series as teams adjust defensive game plans game-by-game. The model cannot update λ within a series; it uses rolling regular-season averages throughout. **Finding 6 — Market efficiency asymmetry.** Kalshi is almost perfectly calibrated on NO bets (+0.006 error) and significantly better than the model on YES bets. The market appears to incorporate Finals-context defensive information that the model's λ does not. **Root cause identified: missing playoff-context multiplier on λ.** The Poisson survival model uses `opp_adj_lambda` calibrated against regular-season opponent defensive ratings. NBA Finals defensive intensity systematically depresses scoring by 0.70–0.91× regular-season λ, with the compression worsening at higher thresholds and deepening across the series. The model has no feature representing playoff round, within-series opponent familiarity, or Finals-specific defensive adjustments. The Kalshi market has this information via informed participant pricing. **This is a feature engineering gap, NOT a model class failure.** The Poisson architecture is appropriate for basketball scoring; the λ input is wrong. **What this finding does NOT prove:** (a) that the anti-predictive pattern will persist in NBA regular season (where no "Finals compression" exists and rolling averages track reality more closely); (b) that the pattern will appear in MLB (different scoring structure). The n=103 sample is a single series with unusual context — ADR-0024 structural adequacy threshold (n≥500, ≥15 opponents) is not met. **Authorized next steps for feature fix (T-072 scope addition):** (i) Add `playoff_round_multiplier` feature to C2 λ derivation — value 1.0 for regular season; to be calibrated from NBA playoff historical data during Phase 2. (ii) Investigate whether `opp_adj_lambda` uses regular-season defensive ratings for Finals opponents — if so, replace with opponent's most recent N playoff games. (iii) Within-series momentum feature: player's scoring in this series vs regular-season rolling average (captures in-series game-plan adjustment). (iv) All three features must be derived from empirical data during Phase 2 retrain — no guessed multipliers. **GG-037 alpha half + GG-004 status unchanged:** diagnosis identifies the likely mechanism but does not close the governance gap; that requires EXP-017 CONFIRMED_POSITIVE at ADR-0024 adequate sample (n≥500/≥15 opponents). T-177 monitor remains active. The DS decision to pursue Option C means that if EXP-017 (MLB or NBA regular season) fires ANTI-PREDICTIVE again after the feature fix is incorporated, the escalation path defaults to Option A (halt + ADR-0004 review). | DS |

Players for 2024/2025 were cached as `[]` before issue was discovered. **Resolution:** (1) Killed VPS process. (2) Deleted bad cache files (`players_2024.json`, `players_2025.json`). Daily VPS feature refresh for inference must use `--seasons 2026` only (current season accessible). Implication: `exp_output/MLB/mlb_feature_matrix.csv` on VPS starts as a 3-season locally-generated file; daily VPS refresh with `--seasons 2026` will overwrite it with 2026-only features over time. This is acceptable for inference quality (most-recent features matter for betting); the initial 3-season data is only needed for model training. For annual retraining, local generation + SCP upload must be repeated. **No ADR required:** this is an infrastructure/deployment constraint, not an algorithm decision. | 2026-06-24 | **[SESSION 81 / T-187B] Per-threshold MLB LR+Platt models: pooled model ECE failure root cause, architecture fix, and t=3 exclusion from active scope** | **Root cause of ECE=0.1246 FAIL on pooled model:** A single `CalibratedClassifierCV(LR, class_weight="balanced", cv=3)` trained on all three thresholds pooled together cannot produce well-calibrated per-threshold probabilities. `class_weight="balanced"` forces equal per-class representation across all threshold values, inflating the effective positive rate to ~26% (pooled average). But per-threshold actual rates diverge dramatically: t=1 actual=54.5%, t=2 actual=18.4%, t=3 actual=3.9%. Platt scaling (Logistic sigmoid) fitted on the pooled distribution calibrates to the 26% average and cannot correct per-threshold systematic biases simultaneously. Result: at holdout evaluation, t=1 model predicts 73.3% (actual 54.5%, over-predicts +18.8pp); t=2 model predicts 35.4% (actual 18.4%, over-predicts +17.0pp). ECE = 0.1246 >> 0.05 threshold. **Diagnostic run (local — VPS OOM on full CSV):** Per-threshold Platt ECE verified by running separate pipelines on each threshold's subset. Results: t=1 ECE=0.013 (PASS ≤0.05), t=2 ECE=0.011 (PASS), t=3 ECE=0.004 (PASS). Brier delta: t=1=+0.0055 (PASS ≥0.001), t=2=+0.0022 (PASS), t=3=+0.0002 (FAIL — below threshold). **Architecture fix:** Per-threshold separate `StandardScaler → CalibratedClassifierCV(LR, sigmoid, cv=3)` pipelines for t=1 and t=2. Each pipeline trains on its own threshold's rows only; Platt scaling calibrates to the correct per-threshold base rate. `threshold` is removed from the feature vector — it no longer varies within a per-threshold pipeline and would be a degenerate constant column. `col_medians` are shared (computed from the full `train_df` before splitting by threshold). Shadow gate: BOTH t=1 AND t=2 must PASS for the artifact to be saved. **t=3 exclusion (GG-042 registered):** At t=3, base rate=3.9% and AUC=0.61 produce a Brier improvement of only +0.0002 (required ≥0.001). Even if the gate passed, t=3 bets would almost never fire — the model predicts ~3.9% while Kalshi asks ~8¢ → edge is consistently negative. t=3 is excluded from `THRESHOLDS` pending T-187G (live SP overlay injection, which would provide meaningful signal for rare 3+ hit events). `_EXCLUDED_THRESHOLDS = [3]` registered and GG-042 logged. **Artifact schema change:** Old: `{"pipeline": pipe, ...}`. New: `{"pipelines": {1: pipe1, 2: pipe2}, "feature_names": [...18 features...], "col_medians": medians, "model_version": model_version, "thresholds": [1, 2], "sport": "mlb"}`. `_mlb_model_version(feature_names)` hash unchanged (features identical across thresholds). **Inference change:** `run_mlb_paper_trade.py` dispatches `pipelines[int(mkt.threshold)].predict_proba(X)[0, 1]`. `threshold` removed from `_build_mlb_feature_vector` signature and `_NON_FEATURE_MLB`. `_MODEL_THRESHOLDS = frozenset({1, 2})`. **Test count:** 9 changes in `test_run_mlb_paper_trade.py`, 7 changes in `test_t183_mlb_c3.py`. Shadow gate expected to PASS after re-train on VPS with updated script. | EL |

Results: train_n=101,400 rows at t=3; holdout_n=25,021 rows. null_rate=3.91%. Brier delta=**+0.0002 (FAIL** — required ≥0.001). ECE=0.0037 (PASS). AUC=**0.6141**. **t=3 shadow gate FAIL — same result as T-187B.** T-187G did not change the training data and therefore did not change the shadow gate outcome. **Root cause analysis — why the failure is structural:** (1) SP coverage: verified 99.9% of t=3 positive events (h≥3) have `opp_sp_is_known=1`. (3) Brier delta ceiling at 3.9% base rate: at null_rate=0.039, the maximum possible Brier delta is ~p*(1-p) = 0.037. (4) Edge would almost never fire: only 487 of 25,021 holdout predictions exceed 0.08 (1.9%) — model_p < market_price_implied = negative edge for 98.1% of bets. **Conclusion:** The t=3 exclusion is structurally correct and not resolvable via SP feature improvement. A richer model (non-linear, additional SP feature interactions, pitcher style matchup data) or different market dynamics (Kalshi price drops below 5–6%) are the only paths to t=3 activation. | 2026-06-24 | **[SESSION 82] T-187F COMPLETE — MLB calibration monitor (PIPE-05C): derive_temperature design, T_global strategy, non-monotonic miscalibration finding, 35 new tests, 1772 total green** | **Script design: `scripts/run_mlb_calib_monitor.py`.** Reads `paper_portfolio_mlb.json` closed positions; filters to active thresholds `_MODEL_THRESHOLDS = frozenset({1, 2})` (t=3 excluded per GG-042); computes ECE per threshold; derives recommended calibration temperature; reports reliability buckets and anti-predictive check. Does NOT write to `calibration.py` — temperature changes require ADR. Exit codes: 0=CALIBRATED or insufficient data, 1=MISCALIBRATED (ECE>0.05), 2=ANTI_PREDICTIVE. **Temperature derivation (`derive_temperature`): `scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar` on log-loss of `sigmoid(logit(P)/T)`, bounds=(0.3, 8.0).** Mirrors `scripts/derive_calibration.py` exactly. T>1 shrinks (overconfident model); T<1 sharpens (underconfident); T=1 is identity. Gate: `MIN_N_DIAGNOSE=50` positions required for derivation (falls back to identity T=1.0). **T_global strategy (key design decision):** Temperature is derived on the combined all-threshold dataset, then the SAME T_global is applied to both per-threshold ECE diagnoses. This avoids underfitting on per-threshold subsets: at ~50 total positions, each threshold contributes ~25 positions — insufficient for stable Platt fitting. The per-threshold ECE diagnosis answers "does this threshold have a calibration problem at the current T?" not "what is the optimal T for this threshold?". Per-threshold temperature fitting would require ≥50 per-threshold (i.e., ≥100 total) — deferred until data volume justifies it. **ECE formula:** `sum_b (n_b/n) * |mean_pred_b − mean_actual_b|` over 5 reliability buckets [(0.5,0.6),(0.6,0.7),(0.7,0.8),(0.8,0.9),(0.9,1.01)]. ADR-0027 shadow gate threshold ≤0.05. **Anti-predictive check:** calibrated edge = `PC − MIP − 0.07 × MIP × (1 − MIP)`; compares win rate of edge>0 cohort vs edge≤0 cohort. Raises exit code 2 if edge>0 wins at lower rate (mirrors GG-037 diagnosis logic for NBA). **PIPE-05C cron entry:** `10 14 * * 1` — Mondays 14:10 UTC (10 minutes after model freshness check). Exit codes captured in `logs/mlb_calib_monitor.log`. **Key finding during test development: temperature scaling cannot fix non-monotonic miscalibration.** A uniformly overconfident model (all positions predict p=0.90, actual win rate 0.55) IS fully corrected by temperature scaling — T shifts P_cal to match the average win rate, collapsing ECE to near-zero regardless of input model_p. This made naive overconfident test fixtures produce exit code 0 instead of 1. Non-monotonic miscalibration — two groups with inverted calibration errors (Group A severely underconfident, Group B severely overconfident) — CANNOT be fixed by a single multiplicative temperature because the two errors cannot be simultaneously corrected. Test fixtures required: Group A (p=0.51, win_rate=0.85) + Group B (p=0.99, win_rate=0.15). At T=8.0 (max bound): Group A P_cal=0.501 lands in [0.5,0.6) bucket, Group B P_cal=0.640 lands in [0.6,0.7) bucket — different buckets, ECE ≈ 0.43 >> 0.05. All MIP=0.05 ensures all calibrated edges remain positive (anti-predictive check skipped → exit 1 not exit 2). **Test coverage (35 tests in 10 classes):** `TestLoadPositions` (4) — skips duplicates/non-WIN-LOSS/None model_p, reads mid_price_at_entry; `TestToArrays` (6) — directional frame YES/NO P/MIP transforms (uses processed pos dict with "mip" key, not raw JSON "mid_price_at_entry"); `TestDeriveTemperature` (4) — identity at T=1, overconfident >1, underconfident <1, bounds respected; `TestComputeEce` (5) — zero, single bucket, multi-bucket, perfect calibration, boundary 0.9-1.0; `TestDiagnoseThreshold` (4) — insufficient data (exit None/False), sufficient PASS, sufficient FAIL; `TestMainNoFile` (1); `TestMainNoPositions` (1); `TestMainInsufficientData` (2) — deferred at n<50; `TestMainCalibrated` (3) — passes at n≥50 PASS; `TestMainMiscalibrated` (4) — non-monotonic FAIL on combined thresholds; `TestMainAntiPredictive` (1) — edge>0 cohort losing at higher rate. **Suite: 1737 → 1772/1772** (0 failures, 1 skipped). | EL |

| 2026-06-27 | **[SESSION 90 / T-194] `mark_aged_open()` design: in-place tagging within `open_positions`, NOT movement to a separate list** | `PaperTrader.mark_aged_open()` adds `aged_open=True`, `aged_open_reason`, `aged_open_at` fields to the position dict in-place within `self._state["open_positions"]`. It does NOT move the position to `closed_positions` or a separate aged list. **Reason:** `_ledger_bankroll()` derives `open_cost` by summing `open_positions[*]["size_usd"]`. Moving a position out of `open_positions` would credit that capital back to the bankroll — incorrect, because the money is still committed (the paper bet exists; we just cannot resolve it). This would overstate available capital and allow subsequent over-sizing. **Boundary condition (>48h rule):** Age is computed from midnight of `game_date` in UTC (not game start time, which is unavailable at resolve time). Only positions with `game_date < today` are in the resolution loop; an additional `age_hours > 48` check against datetime.now(UTC) ensures the midnight-boundary case cannot trigger early. Fixed-noon UTC in boundary tests prevents test failures at the exact midnight transition. **C6 behavior:** `mark_aged_open()` emits `paper_position_aged_open` WARNING to C7 audit log. The position remains in `open_positions` and is excluded from future resolution attempts (caller responsibility — runner skips `aged_open=True` positions). | EL |

Documented as ongoing factors, not resolved points. **(1) Market efficiency is context-dependent.** NBA Finals player props are among the most liquid, most-watched prediction markets that exist — priced by sharp money, sports media, and high public volume simultaneously. T4 requires its own validation track. Registered separately as GG-046. **(3) Kalshi market depth creates a capital ceiling independent of bankroll math.** Kelly criterion assumes infinite market depth. Kalshi KXMLBHIT player prop lines are thin (estimated $500–$2,000 per market). At $1K paper with 25% Kelly, position sizing is $50–$250/bet — within depth. At $10K+ bankroll, full Kelly sizing would move the market against the bot — degrading or eliminating edge before the position fills. The maximum effective bankroll is constrained by market depth, not bankroll formula or Kelly fraction calibration. This ceiling is absent from governance documentation. Registered as GG-045. **(4) The methodology is the product.** Prediction markets provide high-frequency, binary-resolved calibration feedback — uniquely clean for testing probabilistic thinking (unambiguous resolution, short feedback loops, no confounding). The trading bot is the calibration regime; the methodology (build → forecast → validate → iterate against resolved binary outcomes) is the transferable asset. P&L is the score; the methodology is the value. Preserved as a framing note for post-G6 strategic review. | DS |

| 2026-06-29 | **[SESSION 101] Principal vision, alpha taxonomy, and market efficiency gradient formalized as canonical CLAUDE.md content** | **Motivation:** Sessions 1–101 produced a fully operational paper trading system (T1 + T4 active for MLB; T4 NBA deployed), yet no session document stated *why the system exists* or *what commercial claim it is structured to prove*. As Earl noted: "Probably would've saved a lot of sessions." Three structural gaps were identified and filled this session. **Decision 1 — Principal vision:** `## Principal Vision` section added to CLAUDE.md before `## What This Project Is`. Canonical statement: "This is a calibration engine for probabilistic reasoning, structured as a trading bot." Prediction markets are the only widely available instrument providing all three simultaneously: binary-resolved outcomes (unambiguous right/wrong), short feedback loops (hours/days not quarters), and market-implied probability as an explicit benchmark. Corollary: "P&L is the score. The methodology is the asset." If the methodology proves edge rigorously, it generalizes. New sport = new C1+C2+C3, same methodology. New venue = new VenueAdapter, same methodology. **Decision 2 — Alpha taxonomy as first-class architectural concept:** Subsection `### Alpha taxonomy — two distinct theses, two independent proofs required` added inside `## What This Project Is`. Canonical framing: T1 alpha (pregame calibration edge) and T4 alpha (live market latency edge) are structurally independent hypotheses. T1 tests whether historical rolling statistics produce better-calibrated pregame probabilities than Kalshi markets. T4 tests whether markets are slow to incorporate in-game state changes at 45-90s polling cadence. A verdict on one does NOT transfer to the other. EXP-017 is the T1 validation track. GG-046 is the T4 validation track. The ~1,000 evaluations/game in T4 is a structural consequence of the hypothesis, not a target: 18 batters × 2 thresholds × ~480 cycles/game = ~17,000 evaluation slots; at 2-3% fire rate = 50-100 actual bets. **Decision 3 — Market efficiency gradient as binding operational constraint:** Subsection `### Market efficiency gradient — where the strategy is designed to work` added. The system is designed to exploit markets where pricing is inefficient. MLB mid-week regular season (low public attention, $500-$2,000 book depth, slower price discovery) is the target environment. NBA Finals player props (professional bettors, high public volume, enormous liquidity) are hostile conditions — the anti-predictive GG-037 finding was produced in worst-case efficiency conditions. Binding implication for expansion: the first question when adding a new market is not "do we have data?" but "is this market less efficient than a calibrated model can produce?" Additional finding: Kalshi KXMLBHIT depth sets a capital ceiling structural to the venue. At $10K+ bankroll, full Kelly sizing moves the market against the bot; this ceiling (GG-045) is not addressable by improved modeling. **Scope:** All three sections are session-read canonical CLAUDE.md content — read by every model session before any other work. Prior to this session, a model cold-starting on this codebase had no access to these framing concepts. | DS — Earl Ignacio 2026-06-29 SESSION 101 |

| 2026-07-01 | **[SESSION 106 / GG-058] T4 MLB UTC-midnight rollover fixed — merge-in replaces destructive replace, closing the nightly in-progress-game drop** | **Root cause confirmed exactly as GG-058 documented:** `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s date-rollover block ran `game_ids[:] = _espn_mlb_game_ids_today()` at every UTC-midnight crossing, replacing the full tracked game list with the new calendar day's ESPN slate. Since ESPN's `dates=` scoreboard query returns only that day's games, any West-coast game still live at UTC midnight (common — first pitch 22:30–01:45 UTC straddles the boundary) was silently dropped and never polled again, directly suppressing the CLAUDE.md ~1,000-evals/game throughput target for every late game, every night. **Fix (matches GG-058's own resolution path):** Added `_espn_game_status(espn_game_id) -> str` — single-game ESPN status lookup, returns `""` on fetch failure (a failure is never treated as terminal, so a transient ESPN outage cannot cause a false drop). Added `_rollover_game_ids(tracked_game_ids, newly_discovered, status_fn=_espn_game_status) -> list[str]` — pure function implementing merge-in: carries forward any tracked game not yet in `newly_discovered` and not at `STATUS_FINAL`/`STATUS_POSTPONED`, then appends new-day discoveries. Main loop now does `game_ids[:] = _rollover_game_ids(game_ids, newly_discovered)` instead of the destructive replace. **Secondary fix found during implementation:** pregame-context dicts (`by_player_id`, `name_to_pregame`) were `.clear()`'d before `.update()` at rollover — combined with `_load_pregame_context()` only ever loading the single most-recent day's file, this could silently drop player-matching context for carried-over games. Changed to additive `.update()` only; accepted that these dicts now only grow (judged acceptable — small per-player payloads, daily service restart regardless). **Test coverage:** `TestEspnGameStatus` (3 tests) + `TestRolloverGameIds` (7 tests) added to `tests/test_run_t4_mlb_live.py`, including the safety-critical case (fetch failure treated as non-terminal, not a drop trigger). Full suite: 2159 passed, 2 pre-existing unrelated failures (stale Kalshi test-market dates, stale feature CSV — both pre-existing freshness checks, not regressions). **Registered T-215** for this fix. Commit and VPS deploy to follow this entry. | EL |
| 2026-07-01 | **[SESSION 106 / GG-062] Dual concurrent `t4-mlb` processes recurred for ~1h48m — T-210's `pkill`-based singleton guard proven race-prone** | **Finding:** While investigating a "double-rollover, 28s apart" anomaly flagged in the SESSION 105 handoff, forensic analysis of `t4_mlb_live_cron.log` proved two independent `run_t4_mlb_live.py` processes ran concurrently from ~23:31 UTC 2026-06-30 through 01:19:19 UTC 2026-07-01 (~1h48m) — the same failure class T-210 (commit `670b88b`) was built to eliminate. **Evidence:** `cycle_n` is monotonic-only by construction (incremented once per completed cycle, no reset path); the log showed non-monotonic cycle numbers interleaved (`cycle=0029` followed by `cycle=0028`). Isolating the full window resolved two distinct series: one climbing `cg_halts` 878→1632 with `eval=50`/`fired=2`; an orphan permanently flat at `cg_halts=0`/`eval=0`/`fired=0`. `journalctl -u t4-mlb` showed systemd restarting the unit twice, 10 seconds apart, at Jun 30 06:30:35 and 06:30:45 — the probable origin: the second restart's `ExecStartPre=-pkill` raced the first restart's not-yet-registered new process. The orphan survived undetected for ~19 hours until the next restart (01:19:19 UTC) incidentally cleared it. Currently only one PID is alive (confirmed via `systemctl status`/`pgrep`) — the orphan is gone, but nothing caught it while it ran; this was only found via manual log forensics, not any automated signal. **Why this matters:** `ExecStartPre=-/usr/bin/pkill -f run_t4_mlb_live.py` is a best-effort, race-prone pattern match — it depends on timing between a dying process and process-name deregistration, not an atomic lock. This incident is direct proof the mechanism can fail under back-to-back restarts. **Impact:** MEDIUM-HIGH — paper-capital-only exposure (no live capital), but double-counting risk against the shared portfolio ledger for the full window, and a demonstrated blind spot in the project's own operational health check (Step 4 only shows the current PID, not historical overlaps). **Resolution path registered as GG-062 / T-216:** replace the `pkill`-based guard with a proper PID-file lock (atomic check-and-write, refuses second start rather than best-effort cleanup of the prior one), and add a `DUAL_SESSION_DETECTED` audit event if two `session_id`s are ever active in the same window, so this failure class self-reports instead of requiring manual forensics. Not yet implemented — flagged OPEN, MEDIUM-HIGH priority, ahead of the next redeploy/restart cycle (including this session's own GG-058 deploy). | EL |

| 2026-07-01 | **[SESSION 107 / T-212] Data quality contract manifest implemented as typed Python module (`data_contracts.py`), not literal YAML (GG-059's original text)** | **GG-059 registered "data_contracts.yaml" as its illustrative naming; this session evaluated that literally versus the codebase's actual conventions before building.** **Why not YAML:** (1) No YAML infra exists anywhere in the project — `pyproject.toml` dependencies (pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, scipy, jsonlines, python-dotenv, cryptography, requests) do not include `pyyaml`, and `06_CODE_EXECUTION_REPRODUCIBILITY/DEPENDENCY_LOCKS/requirements-base.txt` has no pinned entry — adding it is a real infra change (pip install + lock-file update + VPS install), disproportionate for a ~40-field manifest. (2) `pyproject.toml` enforces mypy **strict** mode project-wide (`disallow_untyped_defs`, `disallow_any_generics`, `no_implicit_reexport`, `warn_return_any`) — a YAML manifest loaded at runtime is untyped by construction (`dict[str, Any]` at best) and would be the only unchecked data-shape surface in an otherwise fully-typed codebase. (3) Direct precedent already exists for "constraint manifest as typed Python," not config file: `_HARD_LIMITS` in `c4_risk_engine/risk.py`, `_MLB_BATTER_COLUMNS`/`_MLB_PITCHER_COLUMNS` in `c1_signal_ingestion/mlb_ingestion.py`. A YAML file would be a new, inconsistent pattern alongside these. **Design:** `data_contracts.py` defines frozen `FieldContract`/`SourceContract` dataclasses and three contract instances (`MLB_BATTER_CONTRACT`, `MLB_PITCHER_CONTRACT`, `MLB_FEATURE_CSV_CONTRACT`), importing `_MLB_BATTER_COLUMNS`/`_MLB_PITCHER_COLUMNS` directly from `mlb_ingestion.py` (one-directional import, no cycle) rather than hand-duplicating the column lists — schema drift between C1's actual output and the contract is structurally prevented rather than relying on manual sync. **Scope note:** intent of GG-059 (declarative, auditable, drift-checkable schema manifest, checked at C1 and C2 boundaries) is fully preserved; only the file format changed. | EL |
| 2026-07-01 | **[SESSION 106 / GG-063] 100% of all MLB Kalshi demo order submissions have failed since inception — surfaced as a byproduct of the Task #2 duplicate-check** | **Discovery context:** While pulling `paper_portfolio_mlb.json` records to check for duplicate tickers (Task #2 above), every sampled record showed `"kalshi_order_status": "failed: HTTP 410"`. Widened to a full-history census: **T1 MLB — 52/52 positions ever recorded, 100% `failed: HTTP 410`, zero successes.** **T4 MLB — 15/15 positions ever recorded, 100% `failed: HTTP 410`, zero successes.** For comparison, **NBA T1 on the identical shared code path** (`kalshi_client.submit_order()`) shows a 73% real-confirmation rate (`resting`/`executed` = 115 of 158) — proving the failure is MLB-series-specific (`KXMLBHIT`), not a credentials/signing/shared-retry-path problem. HTTP 410 ("Gone") is a distinct failure class from the previously-known GG-014 429/503 transient-rate-limit pattern; it is not covered by the existing `(429, 503)` retry logic and does not self-resolve on retry. Root cause is **not yet isolated**: the exact same `mkt.ticker` string is confirmed open/listed by the live `GET /markets?series_ticker=KXMLBHIT&status=open` DS-02 fetch moments before `submit_order()` is called with it — yet the order POST is rejected as Gone. The actual Kalshi response body is silently discarded before reaching the audit log (`kalshi_client.py`'s `_post()` captures `r.text[:500]` but `submit_order()`'s error path only forwards the bare `f"HTTP {r.status_code}"` string), so the real rejection reason has never been recorded anywhere. **Why this was invisible until now:** ADR-0008 designed the local ledger as authoritative and the bot as non-halting on Kalshi failure (paper capital unaffected) — so a 100% external-confirmation failure rate produces zero visible symptoms in bankroll, P&L, or bet-count metrics. The SESSION 95 DECISION_LOG entry claiming T4 MLB Kalshi wiring was "Verified" confirmed only that an order *attempt* was made (`budget_used` incrementing), not that any order was *accepted* — same failure shape as GG-060 (Silent Success Indistinguishability). **Impact:** HIGH evidentiary / ZERO capital (paper mode, local ledger remains G6-authoritative per ADR-0008). But ADR-0008's stated purpose — external Kalshi-side confirmation strengthening G6 evidence quality via "two-level confirmation" — has never been achieved for any MLB paper bet, in either band, for the entire history of MLB paper trading. Any future G6 sign-off narrative must not cite MLB Kalshi-side confirmation as evidence until this is resolved. **Resolution path registered as GG-063 / T-217:** (1) thread the real response body through to `kalshi_order_status`/the audit payload so the next attempt reveals Kalshi's actual rejection reason; (2) isolate whether this is a market-vs-event ticker mismatch, a KXMLBHIT-specific order-eligibility rule, or a demo-key MLB-series permissions gap; (3) re-verify with a deliberate manual test order once root cause is hypothesized. **Not fixed this session** — diagnostic-only finding, consistent with the sequential-completion directive (byproduct of Task #2, same pattern as GG-062 earlier this session). | EL |

| 2026-07-01 | **[SESSION 107 / T-212] `validators.py`'s `assert_contract()` owns its own C6 logging internally, diverging from the `SemanticFloorGuard.assert_floor()` precedent** | **Precedent being diverged from:** `c7_monitoring/semantic_contracts.py`'s `SemanticFloorGuard.assert_floor()` explicitly does NOT call `audit.log()` itself — its docstring states the guard has no knowledge of C6 configuration and all C6 writes must flow through the component that owns the C6 instance; the caller catches `SemanticFloorViolation` and logs it. **Why `assert_contract()` does the opposite:** T-212/GG-059 exists specifically to *replace* three separate duplicated ad hoc schema/freshness-check-and-log blocks (in `scripts/generate_mlb_features.py`, `run_mlb_paper_trade.py`, `run_mlb_pregame.py`) with one shared implementation. If `assert_contract()` did not also own the C6 write, each of the three call sites would still need to hand-roll their own payload-shape logging after catching `DataContractViolation` — perpetuating the exact duplication this task exists to eliminate. `assert_contract()` is constructed with an `AuditLogger` instance passed explicitly by the caller (same ownership model as `SemanticFloorGuard` — it does not construct or configure C6 itself, it is only handed one), so the "no knowledge of C6 configuration" concern from the `assert_floor()` precedent does not apply; only the "who calls `.log()`" behavior differs. **NFR-03 tie-in:** if `emit_validation_result()`'s C6 write fails, `assert_contract()` treats that failure itself as an additional HALT-severity condition appended to the raised `DataContractViolation` — an unaudited pass is never trusted silently, matching the `all_ok`-never-flips-back-to-true pattern already used in `risk.py`. **Net effect:** the two frameworks now have deliberately different call-owns-logging policies for good reason — `semantic_contracts.py` is a shared library called from many bespoke contexts where centralizing the log call would obscure per-caller context; `data_contracts.py`/`validators.py` is a single generic contract-checking utility invoked identically from exactly three pipeline entrypoints, where centralizing the log call *removes* duplication instead of hiding context. | EL |
| 2026-07-02 | **[SESSION 108 / T-213 Phase 1] GG-060 C4 Edge Accounting built: per-evaluation edge-decision sink + run-level `summarize_edge_run()` classifier, wired live into T1 MLB** | **Problem being solved (GG-060):** a 0-bet paper-trading run is currently indistinguishable across three fundamentally different causes — (a) pipeline broken (0 evaluations ran at all), (b) pipeline healthy but genuinely no edge found (0 of N evaluations had `edge_signal`), (c) edge found but every candidate was risk-rejected (kill switch, exposure cap, size floor). CLAUDE.md's ~1,000-evals/game throughput mandate makes this ambiguity acute: at that volume, a silently-broken pipeline and a correctly-functioning-but-quiet one look identical from the outside. **Design — additive, zero-regression:** `RiskEngine.__init__` gained one new opt-in constructor parameter, `edge_logger: AuditLogger | None = None`, defaulting to inactive so all 50 pre-existing `test_c4_risk.py` tests needed no changes. The original `evaluate_forecast()` body (all phase-gate/8-CHECK/approval logic, ~430 lines, untouched internally) was renamed to `_evaluate_forecast_impl()`; a new thin public `evaluate_forecast()` wraps it and calls a new `_emit_edge_decision()` after every call — approved, rejected, or kill-switched alike — so a single emission point covers all ~9 early-return branches without touching any of their internal logic. Each edge-decision record captures `model_p`, `market_implied_p`, `vig`, `edge`, a boolean `edge_signal` (`abs(edge) >= MIN_EDGE_TO_APPROVE`), `recommended_direction`, `approval_status`, `rejection_reason`, a combined `decision` string, and `approved_size`. **Sink ownership pattern:** followed the existing `run_t4_mlb_live.py` precedent (`_AUDIT_LOG_PATH` = caller-owned plain `AuditLogger` instance, not baked into C4 itself) rather than hardcoding a default path in `risk.py` — keeps C4 sport-agnostic per CLAUDE.md ("C4... sport-agnostic. Governs capital regardless of what C3 is forecasting"). Wired into `run_mlb_paper_trade.py`: new `edge_logger = AuditLogger(LOG_DIR / "audit_mlb_edge_decisions.jsonl", min_severity="INFO")` constructed alongside the existing primary `audit_mlb.jsonl` logger, passed to both `RiskEngine(...)` instantiation sites (initial construction and the post-approved-bet engine rebuild — two genuinely distinct call sites at different indentation levels, confirmed via direct read, not a single find/replace). **Failure isolation:** a write failure on the edge sink is logged as a WARNING (`edge_decision_write_failed`) on the *primary* C6 logger, not treated as a kill-switch-triggering failure — this is a secondary analytics sink, not the canonical NFR-03 audit trail; `evaluate_forecast()`'s `ok` return value is unaffected by edge-sink write failures. **Run-level classifier:** new module function `summarize_edge_run(edge_log_path, session_id=None)` reads the JSONL sink back and classifies the run as `PIPELINE_BROKEN` (0 evaluations), `NO_EDGE` (evaluations ran, 0 had `edge_signal`), `RISK_REJECTED` (edge signals existed, 0 approved), or `ACTIVE` (>=1 approved) — plus a `silent_success_flag` (true when >=50 evaluations produced zero edge signals) and a `rejection_reason_counts` aggregation, directly implementing GG-060 resolution-path items (1)-(3). **Known gap, not yet fixed:** `run_mlb_paper_trade.py`'s forecast-record dict does not currently populate a `vig` key (unlike `run_mlb_pregame.py`, which does) — edge-decision records emitted from the live T1 pipeline will log `vig: null` until this is added; | 2026-07-01 | **[SESSION 108 / GG-063 / T-217] True root cause of 100% MLB Kalshi order failure isolated: Kalshi hard-deprecated the v1 order endpoint, not a ticker/eligibility/permissions issue — `submit_order()` migrated to the v2 endpoint and empirically verified against DEMO** | **What the SESSION 106 discovery got wrong (understandably — the response body was never surfaced):** GG-063 registered three candidate hypotheses for the HTTP 410 — ticker/event mismatch, KXMLBHIT-specific eligibility rule, demo-key permissions gap. This session's mandate was to thread the real Kalshi response body through `submit_order()`'s error path first, per the resolution path, before hypothesizing further. Did so: `_post()` already captured `r.text[:500]` internally but `submit_order()`'s error branch discarded it behind `str(data.get("error", data))`; fixed to surface `data.get("body")`/`data.get("detail")` as well. **Actual response body once surfaced:** `deprecated_v1_order_endpoint` — Kalshi has hard-deprecated `POST /portfolio/orders` (v1). This is a platform-wide endpoint retirement, not a KXMLBHIT-specific or demo-key-specific condition. **Why NBA showed 73% success on the "identical" code path (per the SESSION 106 entry) while MLB showed 0%:** not a code-path difference — a timing one. NBA's 158 T1 paper bets were placed before Kalshi enforced the v1 deprecation; MLB paper trading began after enforcement, so every single MLB order hit the now-dead endpoint. Confirmed via the GG-063 entry's own NBA status breakdown: `{'resting': 87, 'executed': 28, 'failed: HTTP 503': 18, 'failed: HTTP 429': 16, 'failed: transient...': 9}` — zero HTTP 410s in the NBA history, consistent with NBA orders predating enforcement. **Fix (touches ADR-0008, immutable — superseding addendum to follow before session close per operator-selected option):** migrated `submit_order()` from `POST /portfolio/orders` (v1: `type`, `action`, `side=yes/no`, integer `count`, integer-cents `yes_price`/`no_price`) to `POST /portfolio/events/orders` (v2: single `side=bid/ask` field collapsing yes/no+buy/sell per Kalshi's published legacy→v2 mapping — `side="yes"`→`bid`, `side="no"`→`ask`, since this bot only ever buys — plus fixed-point decimal strings for `count`/`price` instead of ints, and two new required fields, `time_in_force="good_till_canceled"` and `self_trade_prevention_type="taker_at_cross"`). Schema verified against `docs.kalshi.com` across 5 independent WebFetch calls (create-order-v2 page x2, orders index, llms.txt index, order_direction.md migration guide) before writing code, given the risk of a wrong-direction bet if the yes/no→bid/ask mapping were misread. **Empirical verification (per operator's explicit "must verify with a manual test order" instruction):** wrote a one-off diagnostic script, ran a real order submission against Kalshi DEMO for a live-sourced KXMLBHIT ticker. Result: error type changed from `410 deprecated_v1_order_endpoint` (pre-fix) to `409 market_closed` (post-fix) — proof Kalshi now parses and evaluates the v2 request rather than rejecting it at the endpoint level. Could not obtain a full 200/201 confirmation this session: all 60 currently-open KXMLBHIT markets were for 2026-07-02 games (today is 2026-07-01) and DEMO's `open_time` for those markets had not yet passed (DEMO showed `status=initialized`, LIVE showed `status=active`, same ticker, at test time) — assessed as a timing artifact of testing outside a live game window, not a structural bug, but registered as a new open item requiring confirmation on the next live T1/T4 MLB cron run rather than further synthetic testing. **Also disproven before the real fix was attempted:** the original ticker-mismatch hypothesis — a controlled `GET /markets/{ticker}` against both DEMO and LIVE for the same ticker returned HTTP 200 on both, ruling out a demo-order-book/ticker-existence gap. **Test evidence:** `pytest tests/test_kalshi_client.py tests/test_t164_order_throttle.py -q` → 52/52 passed (no test calls `submit_order()` directly — a coverage gap, not addressed this session); full suite `pytest -q` → 2155 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (stale integration fixture, SESSION 108/T-212 territory), 6 skipped — no regressions from this change. **Scope discipline:** touched only `kalshi_client.py`; did not touch `data_contracts.py`/`validators.py` or the SESSION 107/108 pipeline test files per operator's explicit parallel-session boundary. | EL |
| 2026-07-02 | **[SESSION 108 / T-218] ADR-0039 drafted: MLB-native T4 sub-band architecture, scoping only, no code authorized** | Per operator session-open directive ("T-211 is high priority but requires a new task number and its own ADR... scope MLB-native T4 sub-bands before writing code"), registered **T-218** (next available task number after T-217) and drafted **ADR-0039**. Confirmed by direct read of `run_t4_mlb_live.py` that MLB T4 is a single flat evaluator (one Binomial model, `KELLY_T4 = 0.10`, one 45s poll loop) — the same "monolithic T4" problem ADR-0029 diagnosed for NBA, never fixed for MLB because MLB T4 was built independently (T-190/T-203/T-204) without inheriting the sub-band redesign. ADR-0039 does **not** copy the NBA roster verbatim — it first establishes four structural differences that change the architecture: (1) MLB C1 is poll-only (45s ESPN summary diff), not event-push, unlike NBA's assumed live feed; (2) MLB's core signal (a resolved at-bat) is a deterministic state transition on the resolution variable itself, not a probabilistic nudge like an NBA field goal; (3) pitcher identity/platoon split is an MLB-unique information class with no NBA analogue; (4) PA frequency is slot-gated and sparse (~3.1-4.2/game), organized around innings/time-through-order rather than a continuous clock. Proposes a 10-sub-band Tier B roster (T4M-PROJ [existing flat model, reclassified], T4M-EVENT, T4M-PITCHER, T4M-LINEUP, T4M-FLOW, T4M-BOUNDARY, T4M-ARITH, T4M-STAGED, T4M-CORR, T4M-EXIT) under the same two-tier acceptance model ADR-0029 used (Tier A architecture frozen on sign-off, Tier B roster/numerics provisional pending EXP per sub-band). Adopts ADR-0029's three-layer architecture (continuous eval → staleness-arbitrated queue → C5/C6) and Principles 1-6 unchanged as sport-agnostic; flags the ≤5s kill-switch SLA as requiring MLB-specific re-derivation rather than inheritance, since it was derived from NBA's continuous per-second event density. **New governance gap registered: GG-066** — MLB C1 has no real-time/sub-poll-interval event feed, blocking T4M-EVENT, T4M-LINEUP, and real-time T4M-ARITH firing until a new data source (candidate: MLB Stats API live game feed) is built; T4M-BOUNDARY and T4M-ARITH (poll-driven) require no new data source and are flagged as the cheapest next build. Also flagged (not registered as a gap): the existing flat model's `_AB_BY_SLOT` baseline is 9-inning-only and understates `ab_remaining` in extra innings — a candidate low-effort fix independent of this ADR. **No code authorized.** T-218 is scoping-only; each sub-band requires its own data-prerequisite resolution, EXP, and Phase 8 Activation Gate before implementation, per GG-061's process fix applied prospectively. | EL |

| 2026-07-02 | **[SESSION 108 CONTINUATION / T-216] GG-053's "second staleness source" identified as GG-062 recurring, not a new bug — fixed via atomic `flock` singleton lock, replacing the race-prone `pkill`-based guard** | **Picked up the `run_t4_mlb_live.py` in-flight edit left untouched by the prior segment's commit (`b001441`).** GG-053's reverification (2,120 `CONTAMINATION_HALT` records, `staleness_halts=1632`, 100% staleness on the 2026-06-30→07-01 game night) had been left with an open question: GG-052's timestamp fix addressed one staleness source, but "a second, still-unidentified source" was producing the bulk of the halts. Investigated by extending GG-062's existing forensic method (duplicate/interleaved `cycle_n` IDs = proof of two concurrent processes, since `cycle_n` is monotonic-only by construction with no reset path) to the earlier 22:36–23:26 UTC segment of the same night, not just the 23:31–01:19 window GG-062 already covered. Found the identical signature — paired `C0000`/`C0001`/... cycle IDs, one series flat at `cg_halts=0` (idle orphan), the other climbing 28→716→...→1632 (real process). **Conclusion: GG-053's "second source" is GG-062, same incident, not a new bug.** GG-052's fix was correct and not implicated. **Fix implemented (T-216, previously registered but not built):** `acquire_singleton_lock()` in `run_t4_mlb_live.py` — an atomic, non-blocking `fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX \| LOCK_NB)` on `logs/t4_mlb_live.lock`, acquired as the first action in `main()`, before any shared-state file (portfolio, audit log, staged-order DB) is touched. A losing process logs the conflict and `sys.exit(1)`; systemd's existing `Restart=on-failure` (60s `RestartSec`) retries until the lock frees — no crash-loop risk. Chosen over a manual PID-file because `flock` is kernel-serialized (no check-then-write race window) and self-releases on process death, crash or normal exit, so it cannot leak a stale lock across a restart. **Why this replaces, not supplements, the existing guard:** `t4-mlb.service`'s `ExecStartPre=-/usr/bin/pkill -f run_t4_mlb_live.py` (T-209) is pattern-match-and-hope — it depends on timing between the previous process's death and its deregistration, which is exactly the race GG-062 proved can leave two processes alive. Updated the service file's comment to state the pkill is now a fast-path cleanup only, not the authoritative guard. **Test coverage:** 5 new tests in `tests/test_run_t4_mlb_live.py::TestAcquireSingletonLock` (first-caller acquires, same-process reentrant call, a genuinely concurrent second holder via an independently-held `flock` on a separate fd is correctly blocked, lock is re-acquirable after the holder closes, lock file contains the holder's PID). **Verification:** full suite `pytest tests/ -q` → 2176 passed / 6 skipped / 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (`test_feature_csv_freshness`, local feature CSV staleness, not from this change) — net +5 over the prior 2171/6/1 baseline, matching the 5 new tests exactly, zero regressions. mypy strict: 26 pre-existing errors in this file (GG-065 baseline), none on any line touched by this change. **Governance docs updated:** GG-062 and GG-053 both moved to RESOLVED in `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md`, cross-referenced via `[[GG-062]]`. **Correction made before this entry was written:** GG-062's Status field, as first drafted, asserted "Deployed + `t4-mlb.service` restarted on VPS; single-process post-restart confirmed" — this had not actually happened yet at the time that text was written (drafted in anticipation of the deploy step). Corrected to state the deploy/restart/verification is the pending next step in this session's close-out, per the project's standard against asserting unverified claims in governance records. **Not yet done as of this entry:** the actual VPS deploy (`git push` → VPS `git pull` → `systemctl restart t4-mlb` → confirm single PID via `ps aux`) — next action this session. | EL |

But that phase is over: the kill switch has drilled at 0.34ms, the contamination guard is verified catching what it should, and production cycle-log evidence (the `MILWCONTRERAS24-2` trajectory cited in the GG-076 diagnosis) shows net_edge responding correctly to a real Kalshi price move, not noise. The mechanisms that now actually guard against over-concentration — `max_single_event_exposure_usd`, the drawdown kill switch, the T4 band budget cap — didn't exist or weren't proven when the dedup was written; keeping "never re-enter a ticker" after those exist doesn't add safety, it just under-samples. Under-sampling is a direct hit on the project's central claim (CLAUDE.md: "P&L is the score, the methodology is the asset") — the T4 thesis is that the market is slow to reprice, a claim about a repeated phenomenon, and a one-shot-per-ticker cap measures "did the bot catch the first instance of latency it happened to see," not "does the bot systematically catch market latency." That is a different, weaker experiment than the one G6/EXP-017-equivalent validation for T4 needs an answer to. Earl's explicit caveat: this ruling assumes T-226's venue-coverage question doesn't independently cap throughput below what re-entry could reach — T-226 was already RESOLVED (2026-07-02, this file, prior row) confirming real Kalshi coverage (~6-7/9 games/day) is not the primary constraint and the dedup policy is the dominant lever, so the caveat is satisfied and implementation may proceed. Closing instruction: "It made sense at the time it was done in order to maintain survival. We're proceeding now - apply accordingly." | DS |

Chose the ceiling empirically rather than from the raw mean/median: queried the full 2026-07-02 `t4_mlb_cycle_log.jsonl` (4,971 evaluation rows) for the vig distribution of the 33 rows that actually cleared `net_edge >= 0.04` — the widest vig on any real qualifying signal was 0.24 (`KXMLBHIT-...-PHIBHARPER3-2`, p_t4=0.45, mip=0.15, net_edge=0.051). | 2026-07-05 | **[GG-086/T-240 RESOLVED — `_reconstruct_t4_ledger`'s open-exposure sum was still date-filtered, permanently dropping positions stuck open past 24 hours; fixed to never date-filter open exposure]** Found while sequentially verifying GG-081/GG-083's UTC-midnight-rollover fix against the real 2026-07-05 00:00 UTC rollover (11 carried-over games, exactly the scenario that fix targets): the T4 band-budget log showed `budget_used` DROP from $20.86 (23:59:59, pre-rollover) to $15.86 (00:01:53, post-rollover) instead of being preserved across a carryover event. Direct inspection of the live `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json` on the VPS found the cause: 22 pool_isolated open positions dated 2026-07-02 ($7.69) and 11 dated 2026-07-03 ($5.09) — $12.78 combined, matching the observed drop — were still open 2-3 days past their `game_date`, almost certainly stuck by GG-084's MLB Stats API IP block preventing `run_resolve_mlb.py` from resolving them. `_game_date_window()` only ever widens to `{game_date, prior_day}` (one day back), so once a *second* midnight passes without a position resolving, it falls out of every future reconstruction permanently — not just at the boundary it crossed. Fix: `_reconstruct_t4_ledger()`'s `open_exposure` term no longer filters by `game_date` — it sums `size_usd` across ALL currently-open `pool_isolated` positions regardless of age, since an open position is real deployed capital until it resolves, no matter how many days that takes. `realized_losses` (closed positions) keeps the date-window filter — attributing a realized loss to a specific day's budget is a legitimately dated concept and was not part of the bug. Two existing tests (`test_excludes_open_different_date`, `test_two_days_prior_still_excluded`) had encoded the bug as expected behavior and were rewritten to assert the corrected behavior; 3 new tests added, including one reproducing the real production numbers directly ($7.69 + $5.09 = $12.78, both cohorts must count). Confirmed the `already_fired_game` ticker-dedup half of GG-081/GG-083 does NOT share this exposure — a stale ticker for a game that ended days ago can never reappear in a live ESPN poll (`game_ids` only tracks currently-live games), so it's inert, not a live risk. Full regression suite green (2,310 passed / 1 skipped / 0 new failures). ## 2026-08-15 — T-451/GG-181 RESOLVED: T4 MLB pregame-context staleness fix, live-verified

**Decision:** Fixed and deployed the root cause of GG-181 (T4 MLB cycle-log frozen ~15.2h, `systemctl is-active` healthy throughout — GG-163-class blind spot). Root cause: `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s pregame-context reload guard only fired on a cold/empty start; a long-running (no-restart) process's UTC-midnight rollover could merge a stale `pregame_mlb_*.json` before PIPE-06pre wrote the real same-day file hours later, and the guard never re-fired once any data had been merged in. Downstream `_run_cycle` silently skipped unmatched live players (`if ls is None: continue`) with no halt event, explaining the simultaneous freeze of `eval` and `cg_halts` counters.

**Fix:** Track the specific pregame file last merged (`_loaded_pregame_file`) and reload whenever the latest file on disk differs from it, not only when empty. `+23/-3` lines, `run_t4_mlb_live.py`. Full suite green (2864 passed/0 failed/28 pre-existing skips). Merged via PR #75 → `main` (`bf8c138`). Deployed to VPS (ff pull, two untracked-file conflicts verified byte-identical before removal), `t4-mlb` restarted.

**Live proof:** cycle-log rows resumed 2026-08-15T19:47:02Z with real live game state (STL@CHC, correct `ab_so_far`/`h_so_far`/`p_t4`/`net_edge`), age_hours=0, no exceptions in the restart journal. Outage `2026-08-15T04:34:04Z` → `19:45:42Z` (~15.2h) is irrecoverable — not backfilled, per explicit scope.

**Scope discipline:** no kelly_fraction/sizing/edge-gate/kill-switch/logic_epoch changes. GG-170/GG-177/GG-178 and other discovered issues untouched — registered previously, not addressed here (Hard Rule 11). The diagnostic-only-alert gap (nothing pages between sessions on the GG-163-class probe) remains open as a distinct, unfixed concern.

## 2026-08-20 — T-472/GG-191: ticker-date derivation made series-agnostic and refusal-only

**Decision:** replaced the KXMLBHIT-hardcoded, wall-clock-fallback ticker-date regex (duplicated across six call sites in five files) with one shared, series-agnostic `TickerGrammar` contract in `market_type_registry.py` (`parse_ticker_date()` / `derive_game_date()`, keyed per `MarketType`, MLB `has_hhmm=True` vs NBA `has_hhmm=False`). Every call site now delegates to it and REFUSES (returns `None` / raises, caller skips the write) on any parse failure — unregistered series or non-matching grammar — instead of silently substituting the session wall-clock date. This is the mechanism GG-166/GG-170/GG-185 all trace back to; GG-191 registers and resolves the mechanism itself, not another instance of its output.

**Scope of the fix:**
- `run_t4_mlb_live.py` (3 sites), `run_resolve_mlb.py`, `run_mlb_paper_trade.py`, `run_paper_trade.py` (NBA), `scripts/build_t4_outcome_store.py::group_by_ticker()` — all six sites converted to delegate + refuse.
- KXMLBF3/F5/F7 registered as `MLB_PARTIAL_GAME` aliases (previously unregistered — any live activation would have silently hit the fallback on every record).
- `scripts/run_power_calc.py` now counts and prints unregistered-series drops (`_UNREGISTERED_SERIES_COUNTS`) instead of silently excluding them from cell regrouping with zero visibility.

**Verification against real data (behaviour-change safety gate, satisfied for every touched file):** zero refusals on any currently-live ticker — 2948/2948 rows in `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s resolved ledger, 1764/1764 in `run_mlb_paper_trade.py`, 133/133 in `run_paper_trade.py` (NBA). No currently-live ticker newly refuses.

**Discovery during test-fixing (in-scope, not a new gap):** two pre-existing test fixtures across the suite encoded the OLD, incorrect mental model of the ticker grammar — `test_run_mlb_paper_trade.py`'s `TestTickerToGameDate` class treated the ticker's leading 2-digit token as an irrelevant "creation day" with the year reconstructed from the wall clock, and `test_run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s module-level `TICKER_SOTO` fixture was itself malformed (missing HHMM digits) and never actually matched the ticker grammar even under the old pre-fix regex. Both were masked because their fixtures happened to use leading/date tokens ("26") that coincidentally matched the 2026 wall-clock year the tests were authored in. Both were corrected in-scope (same function/file the task named), not registered as separate gaps, per the established pattern of treating stale-test correction as squarely within the mandated fix's scope.

**Regression tests added:** `test_market_type_registry.py` (+9, grammar itself — MLB/NBA parse, doubleheader suffix, F5/F7 aliasing, unregistered-series/malformed-tail/bad-month/no-separator refusal), `test_power_calc.py` (+4, unregistered-series drop counting/surfacing), `test_run_mlb_paper_trade.py` (rewrote 5/7 stale tests in `TestTickerToGameDate`, +1 new), `test_run_t4_mlb_live.py` (+3, plus the `TICKER_SOTO` fixture fix), `test_run_resolve_mlb.py` and `test_run_paper_trade.py` (new files, +3 each — neither wrapper had any prior test coverage). All touched files green; full-suite run in progress at time of this entry.

**GG-191:** registered and RESOLVED in the same session — see `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md` for the full record (category: systemic blind spot, severity HIGH).

**Scope discipline (Hard Rule 11):** no other defect was fixed in-session outside this deliverable. `scripts/build_t4_totals_outcome_store.py` was inspected and confirmed to already refuse via `None` — it does not exhibit the GG-191 defect class, left untouched, no gap registered.

**Addendum (full-suite verification pass):** the first full `pytest tests/` run surfaced two more stale source-pinning tests — `tests/test_t442_box14_gg166_regression.py` literally asserted the OLD two-arg `_ticker_to_game_date(ticker, game_date)` call text at each write site. Same in-scope pattern as the other stale-test fixes above (same defect class, same file's own regression guard): rewrote both assertions to follow the new indirection (write sites now assign to a local — `_gg191_game_date` / `position_game_date` — a few lines above the write) while preserving the original invariant (every game_date write site must trace to a `_ticker_to_game_date(ticker)` call, never the bare session `game_date`). Both tests pass against the new implementation. Full-suite re-run in progress.

## 2026-08-20 — T-471: GG-190 registered — GG-185's step-function trigger root-caused as "not found," bounded negative result

**Decision:** Register GG-190 (OPEN, HIGH) recording a bounded negative result for T-471's mandate (root-cause the 2026-08-19 strategic-review contradiction in GG-185: mismatch rate is a step function — 0/77 under `cbd09ae`, 532/532 under `687bf9e` — while the 8.5-day VPS deploy gap that explains guard-absence is constant across both cohorts and cannot itself produce a step). Root cause was NOT found within session budget. GG-185's status is unchanged (PARTIALLY RESOLVED) — it is explicitly not upgraded to RESOLVED, per this task's own instruction that resolution requires the actual trigger, not further narrowing.

**Evidence, ruled out with direct verification (see GG-190's full record for detail):** (1) VPS timezone/clock — `Etc/UTC`, confirmed no skew. (2) A `t4-mlb.service` systemd restart at the 2026-08-08 corruption onset — `journalctl` shows zero restarts between the `687bf9e` deploy (2026-08-07T05:26:30Z) and at least 2026-08-10; the process ran continuously through the entire onset. (3) `paper_trader.py` (the ledger-persistence module) source differences between `cbd09ae` and `687bf9e` — `git diff --stat` confirms the file is byte-identical between the two commits. (4) `run_resolve_mlb.py`'s ESPN User-Agent header fix (GG-163) as a contributor — confirmed the resolve path only reads and carries forward the already-stored open-time `game_date` value, never independently deriving or overwriting it in either commit.

**What remains genuinely unreconciled:** `run_t4_mlb_live.py`'s `game_date` write-path (unconditional, unguarded UTC-rollover reassignment, flowing unscoped into `_run_cycle()` and `trader.open_position()`) is confirmed byte-identical between `cbd09ae` and `687bf9e`, and both windows show comparable midnight rollover/carry-over activity in `t4_mlb_live_cron.log`. Yet a precisely deploy-timestamp-boxed query against `logs/t4_mlb_resolved_ledger.jsonl` shows `cbd09ae`: 77/77 midnight-crossers correctly ticker-matched (including writes 1-3+ hours post-rollover); `687bf9e`: 0/532 correctly matched. Identical code, opposite outcomes. This is the open paradox.

**Self-correction during investigation:** an earlier pass this session loosely bucketed crossers by calendar date rather than by actual deploy timestamp, which pooled a third, older, pre-GG-081/082 code era (the July TBJCAMINERO13 double-fire window that motivated `_game_date_window()`'s creation) in with the `cbd09ae` cohort, producing a misleadingly clean "1444/1444 correct" figure. Re-run strictly time-boxed to confirmed VPS deploy timestamps before trusting the result.

**Next evidence specified (not pursued this session, out of STANDARD-tier/one-deliverable budget):** diff `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.pre_gg166_correction_20260807T052850Z.json` (a VPS portfolio-state backup timestamped ~2 minutes after the `687bf9e` deploy) against contemporaneous live portfolio state, for a persisted-runtime-state trigger; and, in a future code-permitted session, instrument `game_date`'s live value at the `trader.open_position()` call site for a paired corrupted/correct comparison.

**Scope discipline (Hard Rule 11):** No code fix applied this session (explicit task constraint — three ledger-write call sites are ADR-gated). No sizing/kelly_fraction/kill-switch touched. GG-185 status left as-is per instruction (upgrade to RESOLVED requires the trigger, not narrowing).

See ADR-0055.` — exact match to target shape. Self-clear/self-fire property confirmed with synthetic clean cohort (0 mismatches), corrupted cohort (mismatch counted), and unparseable-ticker cohort (correctly excluded, not miscounted as a mismatch, per the refusal-only contract).

**GG-197 registered (RESOLVED same-session):** the governance-defect (false MET verdict) is fixed; the underlying data corruption (532/719 mismatched rows) is NOT — that remains gated on ADR-0055's unsigned D1, tracked separately. **Task:** MICRO/one-deliverable, reserved gap number GG-199 only (GG-198 already consumed by T-473 same day). Verified against real `SESSION_CLAIMS.md`: correctly and only flags T-449 and T-463 (both independently confirmed via direct grep to have no CLOSED row anywhere in the file). `scripts/lib/gg_id_uniqueness_check.py` (new) extracts every `### GG-NNN` header from the live log plus archive combined and flags any id appearing more than once; verified against real files: reports clean (GG-187's collision was already resolved by T-468 — explicitly not retro-fixed, per task instruction). Both wired into `.claude/hooks/governance_scan.sh` (claim-lifecycle check after the OPEN-gaps block; uniqueness check after the header/status-line parity block) and the duplicate-id check additionally mirrored into CLAUDE.md's Step 3 itself (not just the hook), per the file's own instruction to re-run the reconciliation in the same sitting whenever Step 3 is touched (the GG-144 lesson: a fix landing in only one of the two copies never propagates). `scripts/new_session_worktree.sh` line 34 widened to `git fetch --quiet origin main '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*'`, fetching every remote-tracking ref on every worktree launch; line 40 (`git worktree add -b "$BRANCH" "$WT_PATH" origin/main`) deliberately left untouched — isolation still starts from a fresh `origin/main` base, this widens visibility only.

**Verification:** 10 new unit tests across `tests/test_claim_closure_check.py` (6) and `tests/test_gg_id_uniqueness_check.py` (4), all passing, using the established `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` pattern (no git repo or live file dependency). Both wired hook snippets manually re-run from the worktree against real repository data (the hook itself always `cd`s to the shared main-tree checkout via its hardcoded `PROJECT` path, so a not-yet-merged worktree script cannot be exercised via a direct `bash governance_scan.sh` run pre-merge). CLAUDE.md's own Step 3 reconciliation re-run in the same sitting: `gap headers=81 status lines=81` (parity holds) and the new uniqueness check reports clean, matching the hook's output exactly.

**GG-199 registered (RESOLVED same-session):** the worktree launcher's narrow fetch scope is the causally upstream defect — it can make a claim's branch invisible to the very session that needs to find and close it, which Assertion 1's claim/CLOSED check can only ever DETECT after the fact, never PREVENT. **Task:** STANDARD/one-deliverable per Hard Rule 11 — diagnose GG-203 (100% Kalshi order-submission failure since 2026-08-15) and fix only if the cause is unambiguous and does not touch sizing. Ruled out, with direct evidence: credential/key rotation (`.env`/`VENUE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` mtime unchanged since Jul 14), `BOT_ENV` misrouting (GG-152 fix verified still intact), broken/deactivated demo account (live `GET /portfolio/balance` succeeds), ticker/market non-existence (live `GET /markets/{ticker}` on the most recent failing ticker returns `status: active` with real pricing), T-472/GG-191's ticker-grammar refactor (deployed 08-19, never touches `kalshi_client.py`), MLB/KXMLBHIT-series-specificity (a fresh non-MLB ticker fails identically), single-ticker cause (multiple fresh, independently-confirmed-open tickers all fail), request body schema drift (differential `side`/`self_trade_prevention_type` testing reproduces Kalshi's own real validation messages, confirming production's `bid`/`ask` mapping and required-field set are exactly correct), and random flakiness (5x identical retries return the identical code every time). ## 2026-08-28 — T-502: ADR-0055 D2 repair of 46 stuck-open T4M-PROJ epoch-12 positions; live-service in-memory-flush hazard discovered and worked around (GG-223/GG-224)

**Task:** T-502/GG-223 — repair the 46 T4M-PROJ epoch-12 `open_positions` in `paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json` whose `game_date` disagreed with their ticker-embedded date, under ADR-0055 D2 authorization (D2 permitted to execute first/independently of D1/D3).
**Decisions:**
1. Built a new, narrowly-scoped repair script (`scripts/t502_repair_d2_stuck_open.py`) rather than extending `correct_t4_game_dates.py` (GG-166/T-429) or `market_type_registry.py`, per the scope fence (`scripts/` limited to a NEW file, no edits to existing production scripts).
2. Verified the ADR-0055 §2 item 1 precondition empirically before trusting either date parser: cross-checked the legacy regex parser (`correct_t4_game_dates.ticker_to_game_date`) against the canonical series-agnostic parser (`market_type_registry.derive_game_date`) on all 46 targeted tickers — 0 disagreements, both parsers agreed on every row.
3. Used a byte-verified backup (snapshot once, write, re-read, compare sha256 + line count + byte-equality — a backup written but not read back does not count as verified per task instruction) plus optimistic-concurrency re-check immediately before the atomic write, since the ledger is actively appended to by the live `t4-mlb.service` roughly every 45-90s.
4. **First `--apply` run appeared to succeed (correct backup, correct write, correct exit code) but was found fully reverted on a follow-up check** — `t4-mlb.service` holds the entire portfolio in memory and flushes its own in-memory (stale) copy back to disk on a periodic cycle, without re-reading the file first, silently undoing the external repair within roughly one flush interval (~22-72s observed). This is not addressable by any purely external safeguard, since the danger window is after the external write completes. Surfaced to the operator via `AskUserQuestion`; operator selected "Restart t4-mlb.service after write (Recommended)."
5. Re-ran the repair script, then immediately `systemctl restart t4-mlb.service` so the freshly started process loads the corrected file from disk. Verified durable across two independent subsequent flush cycles (`last_updated` advancing twice, repair intact both times, `logic_epoch={12}` throughout, service `NRestarts=0` — clean single restart, not a crash-loop).
6. `logic_epoch` was NOT bumped (D4) — confirmed `{12}` as the sole value across all open positions at every checkpoint this session, pre- and post-write, pre- and post-restart.
7. Ran `assert_ledger_invariants.py` (ALARM-ONLY, not promoted to `--strict`, per explicit task prohibition) before and after: 676 → 630 total violations across 54 band-scoped runs, an exact −46 delta matching the repair count. The 14 (band, assertion) NO_FORMULA/unevaluated pairs (T1, T2, T4M-PROJ, UNTAGGED) were identical and unevaluated in both runs — not reported as clean.
8. Registered GG-223 (RESOLVED, this repair) and a new GG-224 (OPEN, MEDIUM — the general live-service in-memory-flush clobber hazard, applicable beyond this one file/service). Noted but did NOT fix (out of scope fence) a doc bug in `04_EXECUTION/LEDGER_INVARIANT_SUITE.md`'s cache-refresh command (references a nonexistent VPS-side `scp` source path); folded into GG-224's narrative.
9. D1 (532 closed positions) and D3 (76 rejected positions) were left untouched — out of scope this session, bundled separately as "Wave 11" per the task's own instruction.
