## 2026-09-01 — T-509: staffed all three ADR-0054(a) §8 named-not-staffed follow-ons (GG-232); replay-harness silent market_type default fixed at its one call site; ledger-invariant and band-monitor tooling made cell-aware against the 78-cell registry

**Task:** T-509/GG-232 — ADR-0054(a) §8/§9 elevated three named follow-ons to required-staffed on 2026-08-26 sign-off; none had been claimed by any session in the intervening five days. Operator priority order: item 4 (replay-harness silent default, PRIORITY — "produces confidently wrong output rather than a visible error"), item 1 (ledger-invariant cell-awareness), item 2 (band-monitor cell-awareness).
**Decisions:**
1. Registered GG-232 as the first commit (per explicit instruction) documenting the staffing gap independently of the fix, before any implementation.
2. **Item 4:** `replay_harness_t427.py`'s `replay_one()` now passes `market_type=` explicitly to `open_position()` instead of relying on the function's silent default (which had attributed every replayed position to `MLB_PLAYER_PROP_HITS` regardless of true type). Went as far as the call site; did not make `open_position()`'s `market_type` parameter required/non-defaulted, since that is a shared signature used by 6 other call sites outside this task's scope fence — per the task's own "STOP and report if [going further] would require changing a shared signature" instruction, this was reported rather than done. Added a test that fails against the pre-fix silent-default behavior. Commit `8e3182d`.
3. **Item 2:** `run_band_monitor.py` made cell-aware. Commit `386c6a0` (post-rebase; `60bd8dc` pre-rebase).
4. **Item 1:** `assert_ledger_invariants.py` made cell-aware against the live 78-cell `(MarketType, ExecutionBand)` registry. Design choice: only 4 of 17 assertion functions (G, K, I2, J2) have market_type-dependent formulas; these now run per-cell via a new `positions_by_cell()`-driven loop, while the other 13 remain band-scoped via the existing `positions_by_band()` path — cell-level restructuring was applied only where the formula actually depends on market_type, not uniformly across all assertions. G/K gated on `VIG_FORMULA_VERIFIED_MARKET_TYPE = MarketType.MLB_PLAYER_PROP_HITS.value` (the one market type their formulas were verified against, ADR-0045/GG-119). I2/J2 (T1 measurement-stake/contracts-cap) redesigned to take `market_type` as an explicit parameter passed once per call — matching how `positions_by_cell()` actually invokes them (records pre-partitioned to one market_type per cell) — rather than re-derived per-record inside a loop with a silent `continue`, which was the pre-T-509 behavior and is architecturally the same silent-attribution failure mode item 4 was created to fix. Absent/unrecognized market_type values counted via a `_UNKNOWN_MARKET_TYPE_COUNTS` Counter and reported loudly (`UNKNOWN_MARKET_TYPE` sentinel), replicating the GG-191 pattern rather than silently dropping them. `cross_path_agreement`, `assert_I_adr0050_stake`, and `assert_J_contracts_cap` deliberately left band-only/untouched — no market_type-dependent formula exists for them. Commit `066bc8b` (post-rebase).
5. **Real-data before/after comparison (VPS pull, read-only):** total_violations unchanged, 22→22 — cell-awareness surfaced no new violation in the currently-live ledger. What changed is coverage-honesty: 4,071 legacy records (~23% of the ledger, `market_type` field absent entirely, predating its introduction — breakdown T4M-PROJ=3201, T1=499, UNTAGGED=369, T2=2) moved from being silently evaluated under the props-only G/K formula to being honestly reported `NO_FORMULA`/`UNKNOWN_MARKET_TYPE`. NO_FORMULA pair count 14→24 and assertion-run count 54→48 are fully explained by the restructuring itself (13 vs. 17 band-scoped assertions/band, plus a new 5-cell × 4-assertion cell layer), verified by manual arithmetic decomposition that reconciles exactly (52 band slots = 46 evaluated + 6 NO_FORMULA; 20 cell slots = 2 evaluated + 18 NO_FORMULA) — explicitly separated from the zero-real-finding violation-count result so the two are not conflated.
6. **Regression found and fixed (own in-scope edit, not an independent discovery):** `tests/test_measurement_stake_t1.py::test_dry_run_synthetic_record_passes_I2_and_J2` broke under the I2/J2 redesign (old 2-arg call relied on per-record market_type inference that no longer exists). Fixed at the one call site (`market_type=rec["market_type"]` passed explicitly) rather than relaxing the new gate with a record-field fallback, which would have reintroduced the exact per-record silent-handling anti-pattern the redesign eliminated. Judged as a same-session fix, not a Hard-Rule-11 register-and-stop case, since Hard Rule 11 governs independently-discovered pre-existing defects, not regressions caused by the session's own in-scope edit, and the task's "full suite green before close-out" requirement is non-negotiable.
7. **Out-of-scope discovery, registered and stopped on (Hard Rule 11):** `04_EXECUTION/LEDGER_INVARIANT_SUITE.md`'s documented VPS-fetch commands reference nonexistent filenames (`.vps_portfolio_cache_mlb.json`-style names); real current filenames are `logs/paper_portfolio_mlb.json`, `logs/paper_portfolio_mlb_t4.json`, `logs/t4_mlb_outcome_store.jsonl`. Registered as GG-235 (OPEN, LOW), not fixed — outside the scope fence (`replay_harness_t427.py`, `assert_ledger_invariants.py`, `run_band_monitor.py`, and their tests only).
8. Did not touch any `kelly_fraction`, cell status, or ledger row; did not implement ADR-0054(b) or (d); did not add or rename any `ExecutionBand` member — all confirmed unviolated at close-out.
9. GG-184 (the pre-existing gap this session's item 4 partially addresses) updated: PARTIALLY RESOLVED, not RESOLVED — 1 of 7 `open_position()` call sites fixed; the other 6 and the shared-signature default itself are unchanged, per the scope-fence boundary in decision 2 above.
10. Full suite green post-rebase onto `origin/main`: 3001 passed / 28 skipped / 0 failed. Branch (`session/20260901T052401Z-t509-adr0054a-cell-awareness`) rebased and force-pushed (`--force-with-lease`, confirmed via `git merge-base` that the rejected remote history was this session's own earlier partial push, not concurrent work). ## 2026-09-03 — T-513: implemented ADR-0054(b) — re-keyed `LogicEpochBoundary.bands_affected` from band to `(MarketType, band)` cell keys

**Task:** T-513/GG-237 — sole deliverable: re-key `logic_epoch.py`'s twelve boundaries from band-string scope to `(MarketType, band)` cell-key scope per ADR-0054(b) (SIGNED, item (b), section 9 sign-off; APPROVALS_REGISTER confirmed). Asymmetric-risk framing binding throughout: a boundary scoped too wide only costs sample; a boundary scoped too narrow silently leaves dirty rows inside a cohort that reports itself clean — scope wide when uncertain, and justify every one of the twelve individually.
**Decisions:**
1. Ancestor-checked T-509 (ADR-0054(a), the prerequisite cell-awareness build DELIVERABLE 0 named) before starting: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <T-509 tip> origin/main` → exit 0 (landed, via T-514's `4723550`/`22e9c2b`). Confirmed via `git show --stat` on T-509's own commits that it touches only `scripts/assert_ledger_invariants.py` and `scripts/run_band_monitor.py` — never `logic_epoch.py` — so the task's STOP condition never applied; proceeded without coordination.
2. Added `CellKey = tuple[MarketType, str]` and renamed the sentinel `ALL_BANDS` → `ALL_CELLS` (value unchanged, `"*"`). Retyped `LogicEpochBoundary.bands_affected` to `frozenset[CellKey | str]` (the `str` arm carries only the `ALL_CELLS` sentinel, never a bare band).
3. Re-keyed all eleven explicit `_BOUNDARIES` entries. Two (epoch 3/GG-077, epoch 10/GG-142) kept `ALL_CELLS` — both landed commits that touched shared, unconditional code with no cell-gate, so no narrower scope is possible or honest. The remaining nine, all band-specific, were scoped to `MarketType.MLB_PLAYER_PROP_HITS` alone, not left as bare bands and not widened to include NBA: verified directly that all twelve boundaries predate any NBA cell (NBA's sole historical cell used bare band strings, never overlapping T1/T2/T3/T4M-PROJ) and predate any second MLB cell (the next MLB market-type cell, per T-504/GG-226, landed 2026-08-29 — after all twelve boundaries, which run 2026-07-05 through 2026-07-31). Per the task's scoping note, a historical boundary is not scoped to a cell that did not exist when it was set; MLB was the only live cell for the full span these boundaries cover, so `MLB_PLAYER_PROP_HITS` is the narrowest scope that is actually correct, not a forward-looking guess.
4. Did not implement ADR-0054(b) as a literal in-place rename. `clean_epoch_floor_for_band`/`is_clean_for_band` have five existing external callers under `scripts/`, outside this session's scope fence (`src/prediction_market_bot/logic_epoch.py` and its tests only). Reimplemented both internally against the new cell-keyed `bands_affected` (computing the most conservative/widest floor across every `(MarketType, band)` cell matching the given band string, treating `ALL_CELLS` as a universal match) while preserving their exact external signatures, and added two new cell-aware functions, `clean_epoch_floor_for_cell(market_type, band)` / `is_clean_for_cell(stamped_epoch, market_type, band)`, as the ADR's actual per-cell mechanism. This is a deliberate "extend, don't rename" deviation from the ADR's literal wording, made to respect the scope fence rather than edit five out-of-scope consumer files; it does not weaken the signed decision — cell-aware behavior is fully available via the new functions, and the old functions' behavior is unchanged (see verification below), so no caller anywhere silently regressed.
5. Verified the "extend, don't rename" reimplementation is byte-for-byte behavior-preserving on real ledger data, not just correct by code inspection: ran both `scripts/run_band_monitor.py --no-c7` and `scripts/assert_ledger_invariants.py` before (via `git stash` of the rekey) and after, diffed stdout/stderr. Zero differences beyond an embedded output-artifact timestamp filename. This directly answers the task's verification requirement ("a re-key that silently changes a cohort size is either a real finding or a bug — say which, with evidence"): for every band/cell observable in this worktree (T1/T2/T3 bands, `mlb_player_prop_hits:T1`/`T2` cells, all `assert_ledger_invariants.py` per-band and per-cell assertion counts), there is no change at all — by design, and confirmed by evidence rather than assumed. `T4M-PROJ`/`mlb_player_prop_hits:T4M-PROJ` could not be locally verified before/after on the T4 ledger specifically, since `logs/t4_mlb_resolved_ledger.jsonl` is absent in this worktree (a local build-artifact gap, not a rekey defect — the file is gitignored and worktree-local).
6. Ran the full suite pre- and post-rebase: `3001 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed, 2 warnings` both times, plus a targeted re-run of the three logic-epoch/band/power-calc test files post-rebase (`79 passed`), confirming the rebase (touching only `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md`) introduced no regression.
7. Rebased onto current `origin/main` before this close-out, per the task's explicit "self-serialising close-out" instruction. Resolved one textual (non-semantic) conflict in `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md`: origin/main's T-514 had independently inserted GG-238 at the same location this session's already-landed GG-237 entry occupies. Interleaved both complete entries rather than picking one side — no content lost.
8. Did not bump `CURRENT_LOGIC_EPOCH` or add a thirteenth boundary; did not touch any `kelly_fraction` or `CellStatus`; did not implement ADR-0054(a) (T-509's) or (d) (blocked on ADR-0060); did not add any `ExecutionBand` member; did not promote `assert_ledger_invariants.py` to `--strict`. ## 2026-09-03 — GG-236/GG-238 instrument-fixes session, Deliverable 1: closed the unlanded-branch blind spot in `check_id_collision.sh`

**Task:** GG-236/GG-238 instrument-fixes session — Deliverable 1: `claim_session.sh`'s GG-number collision check (`scripts/lib/check_id_collision.sh` Rule A, GG-169) could not see a `### GG-NNN` header registered only on a pushed-but-unlanded session branch — the mechanism behind every GG-162 collision this phase, and the mechanism GG-236 already named as the predicted cause of T-513's GG-237 near-collision, which T-513 hit anyway because detection stopped at the current checkout's working tree.
**Decisions:**
1. Root cause confirmed by direct code read: Rule A's two `grep`s only ever inspect `$gap_log`/`$gap_archive` as checked out on the branch running the check — no git history or other-branch content is consulted at all.
2. Fixed `check_id_collision()`'s `GG-*` case arm to additionally `git grep -lE "^### ${id}([^0-9]|$)"` across every local head and fetched remote-tracking ref (`git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' refs/heads refs/remotes`) for the same two gap-log paths, reporting a collision naming the offending branch if found. This is a live per-branch-tip snapshot, not a commit-history walk, so a since-renumbered/removed id on a stale branch cannot false-positive forever. Guarded on `git -C "$repo_root" rev-parse --git-dir` succeeding, so the function's documented "pure/offline, unit-testable without a live remote" property is preserved exactly — the existing fixture-based tests pass a bare non-git `tmp_path` and no-op through this branch unchanged.
3. Widened `claim_session.sh`'s fetch from `git fetch origin main` to `git fetch origin '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*'` (fallback to the narrower fetch on failure) so other sessions' pushed branches are actually present locally for the new scan to see. The rebase target remains `main` only — nothing merges from the extra remote-tracking refs, they are read-only collision-scan input.
4. Found and fixed a bug in my own first-pass implementation before it shipped: the new `match_ref="$(git grep ... | head -1)"` line is a bare (non-conditional) assignment, and `git grep -l` exits 1 on "no match" (the common, correct no-collision case) — under the sourcing script's `set -euo pipefail`, that 1 propagated through `pipefail` and aborted the function before its own `[ -n "$match_ref" ]` check ran, so a normal no-collision call would itself report a spurious collision. Caught by running the FULL existing test suite (not just the new regression test) after restoring the fix from a `git stash` round-trip; a new sanity-complement test (`test_allows_gg_id_with_no_header_anywhere_including_branches`) failed with `returncode=1` where `0` was expected, pointing directly at the bug. Fixed with `|| true` on the substitution.
5. Added `tests/test_claim_session_collision.py::test_detects_gg_id_registered_only_on_unlanded_branch` — builds a real git repo, registers `### GG-9002` on an unmerged branch (`session/other`) only, checks from `main` (no such header anywhere in `main`'s history or working tree), and asserts a collision is reported. **Verified this test fails against the pre-fix code**: temporarily reverted `check_id_collision.sh` alone via `git stash push -- scripts/lib/check_id_collision.sh`, ran the test, got `1 failed` (`returncode=0`, silently passing — the bug reproduced), then `git stash pop` to restore the fix and confirmed the test passes. This satisfies the explicit requirement that a fix without a test pinning the old failure is how the defect returns.
6. Full suite for the two affected test files: `tests/test_claim_session_collision.py` → `12 passed` (10 pre-existing + 2 new). `tests/test_claim_closure_check.py` (sibling suite, same lib area) → `6 passed`, no regression.
7. Amended GG-236 in `GOVERNANCE_GAP_LOG.md`: status line changed OPEN → RESOLVED, Resolution row rewritten to document the actual fix, the fail-then-pass verification methodology, and cross-references to `[[GG-162]]` (the still-open root-cause family — atomic GG-number reservation at claim time remains unstaffed; this closes one specific detection gap within that family, not the family itself) and `[[GG-237]]` (the live near-miss this fix would have caught structurally).
8. Did not touch `kelly_fraction`, cell status, or any ledger row (out of scope by task definition — this is a governance-tooling fix, capital-inert). Did not widen the fix beyond `check_id_collision.sh`/`claim_session.sh`/their tests/the GG-236 gap-log entry — `scripts/assert_ledger_invariants.py` (Deliverable 2) is a separate, not-yet-started change in this same session.

Widened `claim_session.sh`'s fetch to all origin branches so the scan has data.
